old: SIGNUP PATH, read today. The account is created at https://linuxone.cloud.marist.edu/#/register?flag=VM, reached from IBM's front door at community.ibm.com/zsystems/l1cc/ by the 'Try Virtual Machines' link. The form is an Angular template, and its source lists: email, password and confirmation, first name, last name, organization, country (a 242-option list defaulting to United States, with Viet Nam present), a project description of 75 to 500 characters, an optional event code, a Terms checkbox and reCAPTCHA v3. THE PHONE STEP IS GONE. The form in circulation, including IBM's own archived deployment guide, says 'Provide a mobile phone number that is capable of receiving SMS messages', and the live page still carries that block in its source - but it is inside HTML comments, the controller's submit payload has no phone field, and the SMS-code function is commented out. So the phone claim is superseded, and the row is email-only, which is why identity_cost.kind is 'email' rather than 'any-phone'. NO CARD, NO ADDRESS. address1 through zip are posted as empty strings by the controller. Organization is on the form but has no required attribute. WHAT STOPS A SIGNUP: manual review, not a gate. The form's own success message says the request 'may take up to one (1) business day to process' and that credentials arrive by email once approved, and it also has a refusal path, 'We need additional information to proceed with your registration.' IBM's front door additionally states that outlook.com and hotmail.com addresses are currently refused by the registration system, which is a documented, first-party, signup-level failure and the cheapest one to avoid. WHAT IT GRANTS: one virtual server, s390x, full sudo, a public IP, SSH-key-only access, 120 days. THE SHAPE IS STILL UNPUBLISHED. IBM names the flavors LinuxONE-Small and LinuxONE-Medium and never states their vCPU, memory or disk; the 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB figure is third-party and is marked as such. The console fetches flavor values at runtime, so they are not readable without an account. NETWORK: the instance gets a public IP and a firewall that opens only SSH, so inbound listening works but every port has to be opened with iptables first; that is documented in IBM's deployment guide. EGRESS IS UNPUBLISHED; the vendor can instead throttle or terminate for 'excessive network, computing or other resources'. VERDICT CHANGED to trial-only from qualifies-with-caveat. The grant is a fixed 120-day term after which 'all resources will be cleared of your data', which is a trial with a hard stop and not a renewable free tier; the earlier verdict was written when the 120-day term was read as a re-registration cycle, and no page says a re-registration succeeds. An extension mechanism exists in the portal (a service/extend endpoint behind an emailed token) but nothing states that a virtual-server entitlement is eligible for it.
